The test image shows a tomato **stem** with a tan-brown canker lesion at a node junction, with a dead/wilted branch to the right. The lesion appears bleached/pale with some white coloring and seems to be girdling the stem. 

Top candidates based on stem symptoms:
1. Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot (bleached stem, white mycelium)
2. Gray_Mold (tan-brown stem lesions)
3. Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers (dark cankers with rings)
4. Southern_Blight (white mycelium at stem base)

Now I'll view one reference image from each of these 4 classes.

**Analysis:**

- **Test image**: Tomato stem with a tan-brown girdling lesion at a node junction; dead/wilted branch to the right. Bugwood ID: 5528800.
- **Gray_Mold stem** (5528796): Nearly identical appearance — tan-brown elongated lesion girdling the stem at a node. Sequential Bugwood IDs (5528796 vs 5528800) indicate same series/photographer. Matches the KB description: "stem lesions may expand in concentric rings to girdle the entire stem causing wilting above the infection site."
- **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot**: More dramatic bleached white tissue at soil line with black sclerotia — doesn't match.
- **Alternaria**: Microscopic spore image — not comparable.
- **Southern_Blight**: Internal stem cross-section with brown discoloration — different presentation.

The Gray Mold match is strong: tan-brown color, node-junction location, girdling pattern causing distal wilting, and matching image series.
